title: Metacognitive Myopia in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical modeling using the 'ultimate sampling dilemma' to illustrate how skewed evaluative information frequencies in training data generate biased conditional probabilities in bi-party systems.
Conceptual analysis of how a model's susceptibility to repetition in training corpora inflates statistical regularities, specifically linking gendered pronouns to high-profile professions.
Conceptual analysis of how a lack of metacognitive control for redundant information leads to amplified associations between certain racial group names and negative sentiment scores.
Theoretical examination of geospatial bias as an illusory correlation resulting from the model's neglect of sample size and reliance on popularity, leading to the devaluation of non-WEIRD regions.
